USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Not an acute reliever

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A patient taking montelukast develops rapidly worsening wheeze and chest tightness. He considers taking an extra tablet instead of following his prescribed acute-relief plan. Which explanation best describes why that substitution is inappropriate?

  1. It is the fastest inhaled bronchodilator
  2. It directly dissolves mucus plugs within seconds
  3. It reverses every severe attack without other treatment
  4. It is an opioid antidote
  5. Montelukast is not a rescue treatment for an acute asthma attack
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Montelukast is not a rescue treatment for an acute asthma attack

Its controller role does not replace prompt acute bronchodilator treatment and assessment when indicated.

Understanding the options

Montelukast is not a rescue treatment for an acute asthma attack
Its controller role does not replace prompt acute bronchodilator treatment and assessment when indicated.
It is the fastest inhaled bronchodilator
Montelukast is an oral leukotriene antagonist, not an inhaled rescue bronchodilator.
It directly dissolves mucus plugs within seconds
This is not its mechanism.
It reverses every severe attack without other treatment
No such guarantee exists.
It is an opioid antidote
This describes naloxone, not montelukast.
